ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is an AC power supply; the upper branch is marked with currents 10 A and 2 A, and has a 1 Ω resistor; the dashed box on the right is labeled Load, inside which are a reactance X_L and a resistor R in series; a voltmeter is connected across the load, and the reading is labeled 200 V. Reasoning: According to the given total active power of 1 kW, that is 1000 W. The current in the 1 Ω resistor is 2 A, so the active power it consumes is P = I^2R = 2^2 × 1 = 4 W. Therefore the active power consumed by the load is 1000 − 4 = 996 W. The load voltage is 200 V, and the load current is 10 A, so the magnitude of the load impedance |Z_load| = 200 / 10 = 20 Ω. The load resistance component R = P_load / I^2 = 996 / 10^2 = 9.96 Ω. Since the load is a series R and X_L, X_L = sqrt(|Z|^2 − R^2) = sqrt(20^2 − 9.96^2) = sqrt(300.7984) ≈ 17.3 Ω.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify the right-hand load as series R and X_L with 200 V across it and 10 A through it; also note the separate 1 Ω resistor carries 2 A. From the text, take total real power as 1000 W. Compute real power in the load as 1000−(2^2)(1)=996 W, then |Z_load|=200/10=20 Ω and R_load=996/10^2=9.96 Ω. Finally use X_L=sqrt(20^2−9.96^2), giving about 17.3 Ω.
